public_spec:
Title: Invoice cancellation restores reserved stock

Behavior requirements:
- cancel_invoice(id) may only operate on invoices with status OPEN
- upon successful cancellation, the invoice status must be set to CANCELLED
- cancellation must release any reserved stock associated with the invoice, restoring it to AVAILABLE
- no reserved stock should remain tied to the cancelled invoice
- paid invoices must not be cancellable via cancel_invoice; attempt should fail with appropriate error

Edge cases:
- cancellation of an OPEN invoice with zero reserved stock
- cancellation of an OPEN invoice where reserved stock partially or fully differs from line items due to external adjustments
- concurrent cancellation attempts on the same OPEN invoice
- cancellation attempt when stock restore would exceed current available stock (e.g., reservations in other orders)
- cancellation of an OPEN invoice that references non-existent or already-released inventory items

Acceptance criteria:
- Open invoice cancellation succeeds: status becomes CANCELLED and all reserved stock for the invoice is restored to AVAILABLE
- Paid invoice cancellation fails: cancel_invoice returns failure and no stock is altered
- Reserved inventory is accurately restored per line item quantities on the cancelled invoice
- Audit trail records the cancellation and stock restoration events with timestamps and IDs

Non-goals:
- canceling invoices other than OPEN (e.g., already CANCELLED or VOID) is out of scope
- modifying pricing or invoice totals during cancellation
- restoring stock for invoices not involved in the cancellation

Testable assertions:
- Given an OPEN invoice with reserve_quantity across items, cancel_invoice(invoice_id) returns success and invoice.status == CANCELLED
- Reserved quantities for each item on the invoice are moved from RESERVED to AVAILABLE
- Inventory.lock or reservation records reflect zero remaining reservation for the cancelled invoice
- Given a PAID invoice, cancel_invoice(invoice_id) returns failure and no inventory state changes occur
